package_info.why_malicious: The package was compromised via a supply chain attack after a Ledger developer's npm account was phished. The attacker published version 1.1.7 containing malicious JavaScript that, when loaded by dApps, exfiltrated wallet addresses and credentials to an attacker-controlled server and initiated unauthorized token transfers, resulting in theft of user cryptocurrency assets.

execution_context.trigger: When the dApp loads the connect-kit in the browser (page load event)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On page load, the code requests wallet access from the user via window.ethereum, then immediately sends the obtained wallet addresses to an attacker-controlled domain using a POST request, and subsequently initiates unauthorized token transfers from the user's wallet, resulting in theft of assets.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates sensitive wallet information to an untrusted external server and initiates token transfers without user consent, which is a hallmark of wallet-draining malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate connect-kit code should only facilitate secure wallet connections and never transmit wallet addresses or credentials to third-party domains, nor initiate transactions without explicit user action. The malicious code violates these expectations by sending sensitive data externally and automating asset transfers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate wallet connectors may request account access from the user, but they do not transmit wallet addresses or credentials to unknown domains, nor do they automate token transfers without explicit user approval.
key_indicators: Outbound POST requests to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., malicious-drainer.com)
Automated wallet access requests followed by immediate data exfiltration
Token transfer logic present and triggered without user interaction
Malicious code present only in compromised package version (1.1.7)
Obfuscated or unfamiliar code in dist/ledger-connect-kit.js

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to Ledger developer's npm account via phishing.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to publish malicious package version

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into Ledger Connect Kit and published to npm as version 1.1.7.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to downstream projects

attack_chain.action: Downstream dApps and projects load the compromised connect-kit JavaScript from npm or CDN.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in user browsers

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript executes in the browser, requests wallet access, exfiltrates credentials, and initiates unauthorized token transfers.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript wallet connector code making outbound network requests to untrusted or previously unseen domains after requesting wallet access
Automated wallet access requests (eth_requestAccounts) immediately followed by POST requests containing wallet addresses
Presence of token transfer logic that executes without explicit user interaction
file_indicators: dist/ledger-connect-kit.js containing obfuscated or unfamiliar code not present in official source
New or modified JavaScript files in version 1.1.7 that do not match the official repository
References to external domains (e.g., malicious-drainer.com) in package code
network_indicators: Outbound POST requests to domains not associated with Ledger, such as malicious-drainer.com or webhook.site
Unusual network traffic from dApp frontends to unknown endpoints immediately after wallet connection
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor JavaScript wallet connector packages for outbound network requests to untrusted domains, especially immediately after wallet access is requested. Use static and dynamic analysis to flag code that exfiltrates wallet addresses or initiates token transfers without explicit user interaction. Compare the contents and hashes of package files between trusted and newly published versions to detect unauthorized code changes. Alert on the presence of unfamiliar or obfuscated code in dist/ledger-connect-kit.js and on any references to non-Ledger domains.
